title: Mamajek and colleagues: cycle-23 mean total solar irradiance is 1361 ± 1 W/m^2
summary: The resolution's endnote gives a measured cycle-23 mean TSI of 1361 W m^-2 with a 2-sigma uncertainty of 1 W m^-2, distinct from the exact nominal value 1361.
body: Endnote 3 of the same IAU 2015 B3 text says the total solar irradiance is variable at about the 0.08 percent level, about 1 W m^-2, and that modern spaceborne TSI instruments are absolutely calibrated at the 0.03 percent level. It says Cycle 23 observations are consistent with a mean TSI of 1361 W m^-2 (± 1 W m^-2; 2σ). The uncertainty range includes absolute accuracies of the instruments and uncertainties in assessing a secular trend. The nominal irradiance adopted in the resolution table is 1361 W m^-2 with no uncertainty, because it is defined as exact. The ± 1 W m^-2 figure is the best-estimate uncertainty, not the nominal constant. This card does not replace the nominal constant with the measurement, or the measurement with the nominal constant.
